subject: Discovery: Latency & Concurrency bottlenecks — summary + ops next steps

Subject: Quick follow-up from today's infra + latency chat

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the run-through earlier. Wanted to capture the pain points from our side so we have a written baseline before you put together recommendations: 

- Primary app: FinWell customer chat (real-time financial advice) — currently on a mixed self-hosted GPU fleet + managed endpoints.
- Pain: visible stutter and degraded streaming UX when >40 concurrent chats. P50 is ok, but p95 currently sits ~1.4s per token on tail events.
- Goal: get p95 per-token latency below 600ms for interactive sessions and keep cold-starts under 200ms where possible.
- Volume: typical burst concurrency 50-120 concurrent users during market open; sustained baseline ~20-30.
- Cost sensitivity: must not exceed 25% increase in TCO vs today.

Could you confirm I captured this right? Also please include what data we should hand off to speed evaluation (logs, perf traces, sample prompts).

Attaching the infra diagram we referenced. Happy to hop on another 30-minute call if useful.

Sam
Head of Product, FinWell

Thanks Sam — captured correctly, and appreciate the infra diagram. Below is a concise recap from our side with concrete next steps and the data we need to validate options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Recap of pain & success criteria
- UX pain: streaming jitter/character bursts at tail when concurrency spikes >40. Customers report perceived lag even when P50 is acceptable.
- Measured: your note about p95 ~1.4s/token aligns with the traces Alyssa shared. Target: p95 <= 600ms per token for interactive flows; 95th percentile end-to-end response <= 1.2s for short replies (<=40 tokens).
- Concurrency: burst to 50-120 concurrent users (short 10-20 minute spikes). Our plan must avoid linear cost growth during spikes.
- Reliability: seamless fallback to a lower-cost variant if capacity is constrained is required.

Current stack (from call and infra diagram)
- Frontend chat layer -> API gateway -> load balancer -> mix of self-hosted Triton-style endpoints + cloud-managed model endpoints.
- Tokenization + post-processing occurs in service layer. No prefix caching in the serving tier today.

Preliminary hypothesis (where latency is being added)
1) KV cache misses and small-batch scheduling on self-hosted nodes causing token-level latency tail.
2) Cross-region routing for some users introduces occasional 50-150ms network variance.
3) Cold-starts on autoscaled nodes for burst traffic (no warm pool configured).

Concrete options we're recommending to evaluate (short list)
- Short-term (<=2 weeks): enable prefix/KV cache for recurring sessions, increase warm-pool size to cover 80% of typical burst, and route market-open traffic to a dedicated pool.
- Mid-term (2-8 weeks): benchmark Dedicated GPU pools with continuous batching and quantization profiles to meet p95 targets while modeling cost impact.
- Fallback plan: automatic routing to a smaller-quantized model variant when latency SLO is at risk.

What we need from FinWell to run a targeted eval
- Representative request logs (anonymized) covering a 24-48 hour window that includes at least one market-open spike. Prefer JSON lines with timestamps and token counts.
- One or two sample prompt sets (short/long) for streaming UX tests.
- A short trace from your current production stack showing token emission times for 10-20 problematic sessions.

Proposed success metrics for the pilot
- p95 per-token latency <= 600ms across 95% of sessions during synthetic 120-concurrency spike.
- End-to-end median response <= 300ms; 95th <= 1.2s for <=40-token replies.
- Cost delta <= +25% vs current TCO (pilot modeling).

Next steps & owners
- FinWell (Alyssa): share logs + traces and permission to run a short benchmarking job (due: 2026-11-24).
- Redwood (Priyom): run baseline benchmark and propose two configurations (Host/Dedicated) with cost estimates (deliverable: 2026-11-27).
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare a short SOW/quote if Dedicated looks required (deliverable: 2026-11-30).
- Redwood (Sean): design temporary warm-pool config and fallback routing policy for the pilot.
